text:
The corrupted element is most likely **M4**, the PMOS current source feeding the M3 load. It sits in triode (Vds = 0.327 V < Vdsat = 0.575 V) while its mirror partner M5 is in saturation with the same Vgs. Its width (1.509 µm) is about 1.43× the M5 reference (1.058 µm) at the same L = 2.077 µm, but the measured currents match at roughly 1:1 (8.216 µA vs 7.979 µA). That mismatch is the signature of an oversized device pulled into triode. The +20% sensitivity of +30.8 dB gain confirms M4 dominates the failing gain, GBW, and output DC level. The downstream triode devices (M1, M2, M6, M7, M11) are consequences of the output node sitting low at 0.169 V.

This pushes the PMOS load current source into triode (Vds=0.327 V < Vdsat=0.575 V), dropping vout_dc to 0.169 V and collapsing gain/GBW. Restoring W to about 1.058 um (matching M5/M11) should return M4 to saturation."}
